evidence.reason: fetch() binds `previous` before the network read but then, in the CAS retry loop, treats a strict ancestor of a concurrently advanced checkpoint as success: `if ancestor(head, latest): break` returns the stale `head` even though another validator has already checkpointed a descendant `latest`. The function's own intent (lines 612-613 and 622) is that a returned snapshot is never behind validated history; line 622 enforces this only for the checkpoint read at entry, not for an advance during the CAS loop. The concrete consequence: publish() then builds commits on the older base and, if the remote branch is at/behind that base (the rollback case the checkpoint mechanism exists to defend), the append lands, so the next fetch's `merge-base --is-ancestor previous head` test fails at line 622 and every subsequent fetch rejects the branch until manual repair — worse than the clean fail-closed rejection that a rollback alone produces. The smallest compatible repair is to keep equal-head (`latest == head`) as success and, when `head` is a strict ancestor of `latest`, re-fetch within a bound (or reject) instead of returning the stale snapshot.
